slots_and_copies.name: slot_primary
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Game logic addresses only this 0x0000-0x3FFF window; it is kept byte-identical to slot_mirror by construction (every store in FUN_0800078c's copy loops writes to addr and addr+0x4000 in the same step), not selected by a generation counter.

slots_and_copies.name: slot_mirror
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Byte-exact duplicate of slot_primary at all times in both sample .sav files; no counter/flag was found distinguishing it from slot_primary, and no code path was identified that prefers one half over the other.

checksums.name: roster_record_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: Sum the 136-byte record (8-byte header with the 2-byte checksum field at +6 zeroed, plus 128-byte payload) as little-endian u16 words; if an odd trailing byte remains, add it as a plain byte; fold the 32-bit accumulator's carry into bits 0-15 twice (u = (u & 0xffff) + (u >> 16), applied twice); return the bitwise one's-complement of the result masked to 16 bits (~u & 0xffff). Implemented by FUN_0800044c.

io_driver_functions.notes: Raw interrupt-masked single-byte copy loop (disables IRQs via a bitmask OR'd with 3 before copying). Matches GBA SRAM's 8-bit-only bus requirement; only invoked from the FUN_0800078c save-flush path, not generic gameplay code.

Not decompiled (external/runtime helper). Used exclusively as an equality test (callers check return == 0 for 'match'), matching a memcmp(dst, src, len) signature. Also used as a write-verify-retry gate: a full staged buffer is compared against the real SRAM base 0xE000000, and the enclosing loop repeats while the comparison fails.
Not decompiled. 4-argument equality/compare primitive (dst, src, len, extra); used to pick between two backup candidates before accepting a save as valid.
One's-complement 16-bit sum checksum. See checksums[0] for full formula and verification.

Builds an 8-byte record header (length, table id, index, checksum) plus 128-byte payload in a scratch buffer, computes the checksum, then writes the record to two mirrored destinations via 0x080ec26c. Verified writer of the 51-entry roster table at 0x142C.

Structurally similar record writer (compares two backup candidates via 0x080ec2b8/0x0800044c, copies the winner via 0x080ec2b4). Never references the literal SRAM base 0xE000000 internally, so whether it writes into the .sav file at all, versus an EWRAM/IWRAM-only shadow structure, is unresolved (open question).

Top-level save flush / corruption-recovery routine. Normal path: writes 3 singleton records (table ids 1-3) and a 51-record roster array (table id 4) to both mirrored halves. Fallback path (not observed in either sample file): stages a freshly-built blank template stamped with ASCII 'Clr' at offset +9/+0x4009, flushes it via 0x080ec144, and verify-retries against SRAM via 0x080ec26c.
Save subsystem entry point; gated by an SWI/BIOS-flag test (FUN_08001458(5)). Calls FUN_0800060c (control-block reinit) then FUN_0800078c (save flush).

fields.name: title_tag
fields.update_mechanism: Inferred memcpy of a ROM-resident default/blank save template; no byte-level writer isolated among the 126 decompiled functions.
fields.evidence: Identical bytes 0x00-0x08 in both real .sav files.

fields.name: clr_recovery_tag
fields.update_mechanism: Stamped as ASCII 'Clr' only on the blank-format fallback branch of FUN_0800078c; both real samples took the normal (non-fallback) path, so these bytes remain the default null padding after title_tag.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c:264-269 shows the literal byte stores 0x43/0x6c/0x72 at this offset; real .sav bytes are 00 00 00 in both samples, confirming the branch was not taken.

fields.name: header_game_code
fields.update_mechanism: Same inferred template copy as title_tag.
fields.evidence: Identical bytes 0x0C-0x0F in both real .sav files; matches ROM header game code AH3P.

fields.name: build_timestamp
fields.update_mechanism: Same inferred template copy as title_tag.
fields.evidence: Identical bytes 0x10-0x23 in both real .sav files.

fields.name: unmapped_counter_0x6be
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; one of only 4 raw bytes (2 unique offsets, mirrored) that differ between the two sample captures, delta -1.
fields.evidence: saves/hexdump_and_diffs.txt diff section; packet's own cold-reload mutation probe at this exact offset recorded reverted_to_blank_on_mutation=false, consistent with this not being checksum-protected.

fields.name: unmapped_counter_0xb84
fields.update_mechanism: Unknown; the other of the only 4 raw bytes that differ between captures, delta +1.

fields.name: roster_record_length
fields.update_mechanism: Set to the return value of the payload-copy call (func_0x080ec2b4) inside FUN_08000ff4; constant 128 because every roster record copies a fixed-size struct.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c:697-704; verified equal to 128 at record offset +0x00 for all 51 records in both real .sav files.

fields.name: roster_record_table_id
fields.update_mechanism: Set to FUN_08000ff4's param_1, which is fixed at 4 for the 51-entry roster loop.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c:705; verified equal to 4 at record offset +0x04 for all 51 records in both real .sav files.

fields.name: roster_record_index
fields.update_mechanism: Set to FUN_08000ff4's param_2, the loop index 0..50.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c:706; verified equal to (offset - 0x142C) / 0xDC for every one of the 51 records in both real .sav files.

fields.name: roster_record_checksum_field
fields.update_mechanism: Zeroed, then set to FUN_0800044c's checksum of the full 136-byte record.
fields.evidence: See checksums[0].verified_on_samples; 102/102 records matched across both files.

fields.name: roster_record_payload
fields.update_mechanism: Copied via func_0x080ec2b4 from a per-character source structure (table indexed by table id/record index); internal sub-field layout not decoded in this pass.
fields.evidence: ghidra/decompiled.c:697-701; byte-level content observed but not semantically mapped.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Flip record 0's payload byte at +0x08 (absolute 0x1434) while leaving its checksum at +0x06 (absolute 0x1432) unchanged.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If load-side checksum validation exists (not yet observed), the record should be reset/ignored; if not, the mutated byte should persist and surface as an incorrect in-game stat for the corresponding roster entry.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Same mutation as above, but recompute and store the correct FUN_0800044c checksum at +0x06 afterward (and mirror both at offset and offset+0x4000).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: The mutated byte should be accepted without any corruption-recovery behavior, isolating whether the checksum is actually enforced on load versus write-only.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Desynchronize the mirror: mutate absolute offset 0x1434 only, leave 0x5434 (the +0x4000 mirror) untouched.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Resolves whether any code path detects and repairs a primary/mirror mismatch, or whether the mismatch is silently ignored until the next save-and-mirror cycle.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Change unmapped_counter_0x6be and unmapped_counter_0xb84 independently (not in the observed -1/+1 lockstep) and reload.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If these are a visible day/step/energy counter, the in-game display should change proportionally, confirming semantics currently only hypothesized.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Zero bytes 0x0000-0x0023 in both the 0x0000 and 0x4000 mirror copies, forcing all three save-validity candidates to fail comparison.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Should force FUN_0800078c down its never-observed blank-format branch, producing the ASCII 'Clr' tag at offset 0x0009-0x000B in the freshly rebuilt save and directly confirming or refuting the CONFIRMED_STATIC-only finding in report section 3.4.

open_questions: Exact destination offsets inside the real .sav for the table-id 1/2/3 singleton records written by FUN_08000ff4(1,0)/(2,0)/(3,0) inside FUN_0800078c could not be independently located, due to unresolved _DAT_* symbol addresses in this workspace.
